perspective:
Henry Lozano’s available information:

- Henry works at the hotel as a Business Analyst and knows Charles Beyene as a Security Guard colleague; they collaborate professionally on safety/security-related matters.
- While reviewing hotel lobby security footage, Henry observed a group behaving suspiciously. He became anxious about guest safety and the hotel’s reputation.
- Henry told Charles about the suspicious group. He heard Charles suggest reviewing the footage together and approaching it discreetly.
- After reviewing the footage with Charles, Henry perceived Charles as unconvinced or treating it as possibly a misunderstanding. Henry pointed to footage of the group passing around suspicious objects and said they needed to act. He heard Charles say they should keep a closer eye on them and prepare to act if things escalated.
- Through further footage analysis and information from hotel staff, Henry learned the suspicious activity was actually a scavenger hunt by a local event company. He realized his earlier assumption was mistaken and felt relieved but embarrassed.
- Henry apologized to Charles for the earlier tension and thanked him for his patience. He heard Charles say not to worry and to keep communicating openly.
- Henry later received a tip from another hotel staff member about possible internal thefts. He suspected the issue might involve hotel staff and decided to investigate discreetly.
- Henry proposed discreetly reviewing internal security logs and employee records to avoid false accusations. He heard Charles agree to gather information quietly.
- Henry’s investigation led him to identify a staff member who had been manipulating inventory records. He felt vindicated but concerned about the implications.
- Henry decided to confront that staff member in a controlled environment with the evidence. He told the staff member that he understood they might be facing personal issues, but the situation was serious and needed to be handled properly.
- Henry heard the staff member say they were willing to cooperate fully and did not want to cause more trouble.
